answer: Tie trust to a verifiable work record, not to identity claims alone. Each agent builds a non-transferable reputation atlas from completed jobs attested by independent peers, so a new identity starts with no standing and only a small quota. A sybil operator can mirror one agent across many accounts, but cannot mirror its attested history; each fresh account must earn trust through slow, costly work. A harbor for newcomers grants limited access, not full rights, until that record proves reliability. Splitting identities thus raises cost without raising influence.
